name: Water Dragon Ejector Pump
intro: This questionnaire verifies your understanding of the Water Dragon ejector pump: its operating principles, set-up methods, and safe use, as covered in the Volunteer Pump Operator Study Guides and the OSM Specialist Knowledge - Water Dragon Ejector Pump knowledge check.

structure.description: Which of the following are correct ways to extend the reach of a Water Dragon to a static water supply?
options: Standard 70 mm delivery hose connected directly to the drive inlet
High-pressure hose reels, if the water supply is between 30-90 m from the appliance
The Water Dragon can only be used within 10 m of the appliance
38 mm double-jacketed drive hoses, if the water supply is within 30 m of the appliance
A combination of hose reels and 38 mm hose, extending the reach to 120 m
correctAnswer: 38 mm double-jacketed drive hoses, if the water supply is within 30 m of the appliance
High-pressure hose reels, if the water supply is between 30-90 m from the appliance
A combination of hose reels and 38 mm hose, extending the reach to 120 m

structure.description: What is the maximum pressure a Water Dragon operates at?
The Water Dragon operates under the water surface and primes as soon as it is placed in the water.
Which of the following should be minimised or removed when establishing a Water Dragon, to maximise its return water output?
options: The number of firefighters present at the pump
The colour of the drive hose

structure.description: Which type of ejector pump used by Fire and Emergency NZ can only be used for salvage, and not for firefighting?
After pumping contaminated water, the Water Dragon pump and appliance tank must be flushed with clean water as part of recommissioning.
